findings.failure_scenario: On bridgeless unload/reload, ReactInstanceWin::Destroy() (ReactInstanceWin.cpp:1094-1103) runs a runOnQueueSync lambda on the JS thread that calls quitSynchronous(); quit() sees isOnThread() and calls thread_.detach(). The Destroying thread then wakes from the runSync promise, returns, and drops the local jsMessageThread shared_ptr — the last owner, since the lambda already nulled m_jsiRuntimeHolder and m_bridgelessReactInstance — freeing TaskDispatchThread's queueLock_/queue_/running_ while the detached JS thread is still between 'task.fn()' return and loop() exit, calling lock.lock() and reading queue_/running_ on freed memory: intermittent heap corruption/crash on app close or instance reload.
findings.summary: quit() detaches the loop thread when called from the JS thread itself, and Destroy() then releases the last MessageQueueThreadImpl reference, so the detached thread keeps executing loop() against freed TaskDispatchThread members.

findings.failure_scenario: A Cxx module declaring REACT_INIT(Initialize) with the new void Initialize(ReactContext const&, jsi::Runtime&) signature (dispatched by RegisterInitMethod's ArgCount==2 branch in NativeModules.h:1093-1101) and registered via AddModule/NativeModulesProvider::GetModules (NativeModulesProvider.cpp:35) never has Initialize called: the delegate is stored in m_jsiinitializers but MakeCxxModule only loops over m_initializers (IReactModuleBuilder.cpp:159-161). The module runs uninitialized — e.g., a BlobModule-style module never installs its JS global (__blobCollectorProvider), so its JS-visible setup silently disappears. The ReactModuleBuilderMock test harness skips m_jsiinitializers too, so unit tests cannot catch it.
findings.summary: ReactModuleBuilder::MakeCxxModule invokes only m_initializers, so the new two-argument REACT_INIT JSI initializers registered via AddJsiInitializer are silently never run for legacy (non-TurboModule) Cxx modules.

findings.failure_scenario: Old-architecture instance with UseWebDebugger (IReactContext.idl documents JSRuntime()/JsiRuntime() as null when JS runs in the browser): creating a TurboModule with a two-arg initializer (the only in-tree one is BlobModule, BlobModule.cpp:38) calls GetOrCreateContextRuntime(context, nullptr) -> TryGetOrCreateContextRuntime returns nullptr -> VerifyElseCrashSz('JSI runtime is not available') in JsiApiContext.cpp:90 -> process crash on module creation. Before this change, BlobTurboModule::Initialize used ExecuteJsi, whose null-runtime path silently skipped the block.
findings.summary: TurboModuleBuilder::AddJsiInitializer passes GetInner().JsiRuntime() straight into GetOrCreateContextRuntime, which VerifyElseCrashes on a null runtime handle, whereas the replaced ExecuteJsi-based code silently skipped initialization when no JSI runtime existed.

findings.failure_scenario: Thread T calls MessageQueueThreadImpl::runOnQueueSync and passes the isRunning() check; concurrently Destroy's JS-thread lambda runs quitSynchronous(), setting running_=false; T then reaches runAsync (line 61-64), which early-returns without queueing the task, so the wrapper lambda's promise.set_value() never executes and promise.get_future().wait() (line 79) blocks T forever. The same silent-drop makes MessageQueueThreadImpl::runOnQueueSync a no-op once the thread is stopped, so a Destroy that interleaves with a prior quit (or any cleanup relying on that lambda, including m_whenDestroyed.SetValue()) deadlocks — hang on unload/reload.
findings.summary: TaskDispatchThread::runSync blocks forever if runAsync silently drops the task, because runAsync early-returns when running_ is false and the promise is never set.
